utterances.text: Just before this roadblock was placed, were there any incidents, any major incidents between the members of the two respective parties?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: Well, no major incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Do you know why your superior, Sefkija Djidic, replaced Zahid Ahmic and, in a way, accused him of being responsible for the exchange of gunfire at the roadblock?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: That is not correct. He was not replaced because of that. He was replaced on account of other things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Can we know why?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: Well, I don't want to go into all of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Kalco, what was the situation like in Stari Vitez with regard to arms supplies on the eve of the conflict, for example, on the 15th of April 1993? Let us break this down into several questions. What kind of weapons did you have?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: Small arms, automatic, semi-automatic rifles, hunting rifles, mortars, 60 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: According to my information, you had three or four 60-millimetre mortars?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: We had two.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You had one 82-millimetre mortar?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You had three snipers, out of which one was a Steyer 7.9?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: Only one. Only one. And the other two were rifles that we called Tandzera M-48 from the Second World War. A good marksman could use them like a sniper.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So it did not even have a sight?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: No. No. No. They did not have a sight at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. But they could be used as snipers?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You also had an M-84 machine gun?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You had at least six M-53's, right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: No. Just three.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. They are the 7.9-millimetre calibre ones, right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And you also said that you had small arms, and you had a total of 270 soldiers that were armed?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: We had 256. And not all of them had arms. We had 200 military weapons, and the rest were hunting rifles. However, when the war ended, we had over 300 weapons, because we had taken quite a few from the HVO during the fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Two offensive attempts were made by the opposing side to take Stari Vitez, one was on the 16th of April, the one that you described, and the other one was in August, on the 18th of August. You spoke about that today. In addition to that, were there any other offensives, or was the front line stabilised?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: The first was on the 16th, the other one was on the 18th. And then in July, on the 18th, there were other attempts as well, especially from the garages in Novi Vitez. But that did not succeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: After the month of July, there weren't any serious changes in -- major changes on the front line, were there?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: No, there weren't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: As for food supplies and ammunition supplies, you did have some supplies, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you. You should know, and the Honourable Judges should know, and Cerkez and the rest, we had enough food for the population and for the army. We did not have sugar, we did not have oil. We had ammunition. As for shells, we had those for RB mortars. We had 100 shells for them. And then we used 90, and there were 10 at the end of the war. We used ammunition only when we had to. But we bought ammunition from HVO soldiers. Let this be known. Let this be known. We gave quite a bit of money for that, but we purchased ammunition from them in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: During those 11 months of siege, did you have some supplies coming in, at least from time to time?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: Yes. In the beginning. And afterwards, when the war was almost over.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: When you are saying the beginning, you are talking about the supplies that came by river?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: No. No. I am talking about the assistance we received from humanitarian organisations. The river transport was different.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Was that a different line of transportation?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: No, I am not saying it's a different line. I am saying it's a different story, and I don't want to go into it here and now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. But you opened some routes for new supplies; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Please, I would like to go back to something for a second. I omitted to mention something. In a statement that you made to the investigators of this Tribunal earlier on, that is to say on the 15th and 16th of July '95, when you spoke about the roadblock on the 20th of October and about that fighting, at one point you said explicitly, I am going to read this sentence, "The only person authorised by the HVO of the Municipality of Vitez to issue an order for attacking Ahmici on the 20th of October in 1992, was the President of the Municipality of Vitez, Ivica Santic."

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: Can I comment on it now?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes, please go ahead. First of all -- well, first things first. Is this exactly what you stated?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: Yes. But let me tell you, the HVO, the military and the civilian authorities, were one single command, and that is the Croatian Defence Council, civilian and military. And now, who Santic received orders from, that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kalco, we unwittingly opened a new area now, but I'll have to clarify it. I shall try to simplify things as much as possible. The HVO was the executive branch of the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna, the executive government, right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Secondly, that the HVO, that is to say that this executive branch had two branches of government, the military and the civilian. Do we agree on that?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you. They did both.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I suggest that we move one step at a time. Was there a division into the military and civilian branches?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: I don't know, but there should be, in my opinion, but I'm not sure. I don't know what the actual set-up was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You don't know what the actual set-up was. But since you are claiming not to be aware of the actual set-up, Mr. Kalco, then how could you claim that Cerkez, in 1992, was chief of staff of the HVO in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: Because we received documents signed by him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: May I remind you, Mr. Kalco, that during 1992, all the way up to the month of October, Marijan Skopljak was a commander of staff in HVO in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: Yes, but that was the office for defence preparations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But then before Marijan Skopljak, who was commander of this office? Can you remember that?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And what about Stipo Krizanovic, wasn't he there?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: Well, yes. Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So there is one line, that is the defence department, Stipo Krizanovic, and then Mario Skopljak later took that office. And you will agree with me that this is the staff of the HVO, we are talking about 1992, you communicated with him and you knew him as the Territorial Defence. You confirmed to us that you cooperated with him in terms of the different shifts in Turbe. They took care of this. They took care of this organisation of the HVO army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. They also gave men for this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Cerkez worked there, right? He is one of Marijan Skopljak's men in 1992; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. But from a military point of view, he commanded that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. But now we are talking about 1992. Please, Marijan Skopljak, was he Cerkez's boss, all the way up to October 1992?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And what you said to us earlier on, the Prosecutor did not ask you about the exact point in time, but I'm going to ask you now. Sometime towards the end of 1992, in October 1992, Marijan Skopljak became head of the Defence Department for the municipality of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: Well, that's the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: Well, that's the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But the difference is that they gave it a different name because of this reorganisation?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: But they did the same job.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. But do you agree that it was a bit of reorganisation, that they gave it a new name even?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: Yes, but for the same purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Specifically --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Kovacic, I'm not sure that we are being helped by all this detail. You've got the point of what the witness said. Let's move on to something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I want to really not bother you, but it is really important to distinguish who is who. There is only one question and I'm closed with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Ask the question and then move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: If you remember, Mr. Kalco, at that time, this is approximately October 1992, these HVO people, they called it the municipal HVO government; is that correct? That is the term that was then introduced?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, do you agree that Ivica Santic was mayor of the town?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And then he took over the office of the civilian structure of the HVO in Vitez. What about Ivica Santic; did you ever see him in uniform?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: I never did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned the incident in May, that is to say, the killing of Samir Trako. I have just two short questions. Did you hear of an investigating judge from Zenica having been there to carry out investigation on site?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: No, no, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So you only heard about the military representatives of both sides?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Ours was led by Dugalic, and the other --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did you hear about this being discussed this same night at the meeting of the crisis staff?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: Yes, yes, but the crisis staff is a double-edged sword. It was just a lot of talk, but nothing was actually done.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. You said to us here today that Ivan Budimir was the military police, and you put him under Cerkez' control. I would have to put a few questions to you because you know the organisational structure, but perhaps it wasn't put very clearly. What was the post held by Ivan Budimir in 1992?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: He was commander of the military police, and the military police and the brigades -- and the staffs, rather.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kalco, we're talking about 1992. Edib Zlotrg, your colleague who testified here, a policeman himself, that is to say, he had frequent contact with Budimir?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: He explicitly stated here in some documents that were tendered that Ivan Budimir was commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you've got the evidence from another witness, you don't need to put it to this one. Why argue with the witnesses all the time? You've got the evidence. Now, there's no need to go over it all again. Now, I suggest that we move on to something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Today you also testified about some alleged killings that were allegedly committed by Perica Vukadinovic on the 19th of November, 1992, and you also established that he was a member of the brigade. We agreed before that there was no brigade in 1992.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: There was the defence staff of the HVO, and he was there, and Mario was his commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that he was one of the men who was in those shifts that we had discussed?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: Well, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Can you deny that Perica Vukadinovic was a member of the regional military police?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: I know that his commander was Mario, and the man who saw him shoot recognised that he was the one who was shooting at them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kalco, when was Mario his commander?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: In October, November, and before that.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: Yes, in '92, and after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. You said that there was an armed attack on the logistics base of the BH army, that is, TO in Vitez, during the meeting. Who was it? Vitezovi, you said?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So those were Vitezovi?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And it has nothing to do with Cerkez at the time?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: I believe it does not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Maybe just two or three questions about the meetings, about the negotiations. On at least two occasions, you said that among others, there was also Ivica Santic in addition to Cerkez. Who is superior to whom?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: In military terms, Mario.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But a little while ago, you agreed that only Santic could issue such an order?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: Yes. Santic would come with Mario and talk about the removal of the roadblock, and Mario said, "If you don't, then Vitez will be butchered."

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Kalco, you say that Cerkez said that, but was it within the context of explaining the situation and making it clear that everything might go to hell, or do you think it was a threat, or what?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: I think it was a threat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But was there any talk about the possible consequences if the situation was not resolved by some peaceful means?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: No. It was only said that Vitez would be butchered or, rather, that part inhabited by Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: My next question also has to do with Cicko Bralo, whom you mentioned. Just one thing for the time being, and after that I will show you -- rather tomorrow morning I will show you a document which we're having copied now. At the time when Salkic was murdered, Bralo belonged to a different unit. What do you say? He was the member of what unit at the time of this murder? I'm referring to February '93.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: He was a member of the Vitez Brigade. But of course you can find a different list that says something else, but I could not accept that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kalco, another question. You yourself said that at that time, the Vitez Brigade did not exist at that time?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: Don't harp on the Vitez Brigade. There is his signature, when Mario asked, "Here is a document requesting equipment for special-purpose forces," and it's his signature on it, so don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I don't want to go into a discussion with you. I will ask you a question about this document. Do you have some specific information, apart from what your informers told you, that at that time, that is, early '93, Bralo was a member of a unit commanded by Mario Cerkez?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: I have information from my intelligence officers, and I trust them. I believe that that was so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But you yourself did not see a document, some other evidence?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Since you mentioned this Document 221 signed by Mario Cerkez, and it says, "The municipal staff, 19 September," the municipal staff is supposed to resolve the logistics problems for the troops there?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: Yes. But is it with the use of forces?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. That concept that you told us, and you said that you inherited the JNA concept regarding the subordination of units in a territory, tell us first -- this will be a question -- do you agree that in the territory of the municipality of Vitez towards the end of '92 onward, at any time there were several different units?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the seat of the command, of the HVO [inaudible] command, was in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: In the hotel?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You said yourself that in Vitez, there was a unit which in 1992 was called HOS and then changed its name and became the Vitezovi under Darko Kraljevic's command, and that they were active in Vitez throughout; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: Let me tell you --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. Just a moment. The Prosecutor may ask you other questions about that. Will you confirm that that unit existed in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Was Vitez the headquarters for the regional police of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did this military police have two mobile offensive squads, one of which was called Jokeris?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And in late '92, did the Ludvig Pavlovic Unit come to the territory of the municipal?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: With those oak leaves, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did Bruno Busic ever come there?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: On the 16th of April, were there also parts of the Frankopan along the edges to the east, towards Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: I don't know all those who were there, but I can say about the attack on Stari Vitez, that the responsibility for it is borne by the Vitez Brigade and its commander. Whether he received his orders to do that and in that way is another matter. But all the units which took part in the attack which were inferior to him, what was their supreme commander because they are attached to him. And other units which are also attached to that unit are placed under the command of the commander of that particular formation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: That is a model?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: Yes, that is a model. Now, how it happened --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes. But that model, depending on the instructions of the commander, of the higher commander, could also be different, could change, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: It could, yes. I do not question that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. Have you ever seen a document, an order, an instruction to indicate that the first model was being applied?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacic, when you come to a convenient moment, we'll adjourn until the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, Your Honour, I think it will be just a good moment, because I'm about to go into a new area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: How much longer do you anticipate more with this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I think I could be done that in an hour and a half, not more than two. But I'm trying to be on the safe side, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, try and do it in an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I can assure you I will do all the best.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, the length of the cross-examination of this witness creates some potential problems. We have a witness, Brigadier Hayes, who we don't forecast will take very long in chief or in cross-examination. He certainly won't be long in chief if we're allowed to put in his summary as his evidence in chief. But he has to be on an aeroplane tomorrow afternoon and has to leave for that aeroplane at 4. We were wondering whether it was appropriate to interpose him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's see how we get on tomorrow, if we can complete the cross-examination. Mr. Sayers, do you anticipate being very long?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I would not anticipate more than a half an hour, Your Honour, at the maximum. And I'll try to keep it less than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I would have thought there is time to fit the Brigadier in.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And indeed I have one other witness as well, but after the Brigadier is gone, if we sit till 5.15 or 5.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. Mr. Kalco, I'm afraid you'll have to come back tomorrow, but we'll conclude your evidence then. If you could be back, please, at 9?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KALCO
